glossary.definition: A measure of a bond price's sensitivity to changes in interest rates.
A move where longer-dated yields rise relative to shorter-dated yields, or shorter-dated yields fall relative to longer-dated yields.
The market-implied inflation rate derived from nominal Treasury yields and inflation-linked bond yields.
The expected return from holding a position if spot prices and yield curves are unchanged.
The spread embedded in swapping funding between two currencies, often used as a stress and funding indicator.
The extra yield a borrower pays over a comparable low-risk benchmark to compensate investors for credit and liquidity risk.
A credit default swap, a derivative used to transfer or hedge default risk.
A portfolio approach that allocates risk more evenly across asset classes rather than allocating capital evenly.
Compensation investors may require for holding longer-maturity bonds instead of rolling short-term debt.
A recurring payment between perpetual futures longs and shorts that helps keep futures prices close to spot.
A crypto token designed to maintain a stable value against a reference asset such as the US dollar.
Observable blockchain transaction activity used as one input in digital asset market analysis.
